summary: Lake Superior light off the western entrance to Nipigon Bay, put in operation 15 May 1877; steel skeletal tower of 1961, de-staffed 1990.

lens.note: 4th order 360 degree French lens installed 1909-10 to replace the original catoptric light

access.note: Accessible only by boat. Site open, tower closed.

events.note: Wooden square tower of 46 ft with a keeper's dwelling attached; contract to Joseph White, 1875
Fixed white catoptric light, put in operation 15 May 1877
Practically rebuilt after continued leaks, at a cost of $818.46

4th order 360 degree French lens and diamond vapour installation replaced the catoptric light, reported in the 1909-10 report (fiscal year ended March 1910; the year of the change within that fiscal year is not given)
Air diaphone began operation on 20 September 1928 in a building nearer the shore
Fixed white changed to a flash every 25 seconds
Keeper Arthur J. Newman died of a heart attack during a storm on 28 November 1951 (LighthouseFriends; not checked against a newspaper)
Forty-foot square skeletal tower replaced the original lighthouse; a new keeper's dwelling was built on the island

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27 (independent pass). (1) Andrew Alexander: confirmed on the page images in three tables: 1906-07 (printed p.163, scan 172; 'Alexander, Andrew', Lamb Island, appointed 26 April 1897 at $500), 1909-10 (printed p.170, scan 177; Lamb Island, April 26, 1897, $555) and 1911-12 (printed p.247, scan 254; Lamb Island, April 26, 1897, $680). The 1909-10 OCR puts name and salary on one line; the 1911-12 and 1906-07 readings are by position and are confirmed on the images. (2) The 1909-10 lens sentence is quoted in full from the Lamb Island entry (the OCR prints the station as 'Lamh Island'). The lens change falls in the 1909-10 report's fiscal year (ended March 1910); the exact year is not given, so the event keeps 1909 with a note. (3) Bayfield (1907-08 survey section): the passage says 'About May 15, Captain Fred. Anderson, with the steamer Bayfield, resumed operations on Lake Superior.' The survey report does not state the year in the passage, and the survey narrative's fiscal-year sense is unclear, so the story gives no year. The passage describes the coast between Lamb Island and Jackfish Bay, not the light. (4) LighthouseFriends (secondary) quotes the 1877 and 1878 departmental reports. These are outside the corpus and were not checked. The 1877 quotation is used only as LighthouseFriends prints it. (5) Record correction: tower height 13.6 m proposed for 12 m (Lighthouse Directory; LighthouseFriends says forty feet). (6) Keeper's dwelling: the Directory calls the two-storey wood keeper's house part of the original station; LighthouseFriends dates a new keeper's dwelling to 1961. The story does not date the wood house. (7) Living people: Ralph Miller through Charles Lorne Gibson (roster after 1952) are named only as LighthouseFriends prints the roster, with no personal detail; Mabel Newman's letters are left out. (8) Newspaper check for the 1951 death was not possible here (Canadian titles are outside Chronicling America); the death is stated as LighthouseFriends' account only.
